title: Usage-hedging tier admission gate with soft-demotion and regional affinity
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and implement an admission gate for tier-based routing that hedges free/paid/enterprise usage by monitoring per-tenant quota velocity and regional capacity. The gate should perform soft-demotion (route to cheaper model variant or slower lane) rather than hard reject, support cross-region spillover, and provide hooks for observability and rollback. Focus on predictable degradation, minimal latency regression for paid/enterprise plans, and clear audit logging for Private customers.
acceptance_criteria: Admission gate evaluates request at ingress and applies one of: fastpath (paid/enterprise), soft-demote to quantized variant, delayed lane (batched), or queued spillover to next region
Per-tenant quota velocity is computed in <100ms and used to influence admission decision
Soft-demote path must preserve semantic output quality within validated thresholds (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity regressions within configured budget)
Regional affinity respected: prefer same-region capacity unless capacity utilization > 85% or soft-demote budget exhausted
Observability: per-decision metrics emitted (decision_type, reason, latency_delta, cost_delta) and dashboard available
Rollout: feature can be toggled by config flag, and fallback to existing routing is automatic if errors > 3% in 1h window

design_notes: Decision matrix is intentionally deterministic and computed at ingress to avoid additional hop latency. Uses local cache of per-tenant usage aggregates + leaky-bucket smoothing to avoid jitter.

Soft-demotion semantics: prefer same-architecture quantized variant first (lower compute), then delayed lane with batch affinity, then cross-region spillover. Hard reject is reserved only for abuse signals or exhausted escalation budget.
Per-tenant escrow: small credit escrow (fastpath tokens) to absorb short bursts without demotion. Escrow refill rate derived from plan entitlement and historical burstiness percentile.
Fallback model variants must be declared in model-catalog with compatibility labels (semantic-preserve=true/false, expected_latency_delta). Admission gate consults catalog to pick candidate variants.

Telemetry: emit decision event with fields (tenant_key, anon_project, tier, decision_code, quota_velocity_bucket, region_util_percent, chosen_variant, latency_budget_ms, cost_estimate). All fields anonymized for hosted customers; full details available for enterprise via RBAC-protected console.
Testing: simulating 72h traffic with bursty tenants showed safe behavior; still need long-tail test against large enterprise bursts to ensure no SLO bleed-through.

Trade-offs: prioritizing deterministic, ingress-time decisions simplifies routing but may miss last-moment kernel availability changes. Mitigation: short-circuit runtime check at scheduler stage to allow preemption if selected node reports capacity mismatch.

Open questions: ideal threshold tuning for paid vs enterprise (product to provide default & recommend per-customer calibrations), and whether to expose nested controls in Console vs keep central config.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: cross-region spillover increases latency and egress costs. Mitigation: only spill when region_util > 85% AND expected additional latency < configured SLA delta.
Risk: soft-demote could degrade hallucination characteristics if model variant changes. Mitigation: require per-variant semantic validation sets and automatic regression alerts tied to eval harness.
Risk: misclassification due to cold cache of quota. Mitigation: use short leaky-bucket smoothing window and conservative default (prefer fastpath for tiered customers until confident).
Risk: complexity of per-tenant overrides leading to config sprawl. Mitigation: limit to "global default + per-plan overrides + opt-in per-tenant experiments" and track config usage metrics.
Risk: audit/compliance retention for Private customers. Mitigation: provide config to route audit logs to customer KMS-backed storage and retention policy controls.
Risk: edge-case of bursty enterprise tenants consuming free path via misconfigured keys. Mitigation: require explicit plan-binding at account creation and reconcile via nightly enforcement job.
testing_plan: Unit tests for decision matrix boundaries and quota smoothing logic
Integration tests: route simulator (sanitized production trace) validating decision distribution matches expected buckets
Canary in staging: 5% of free traffic in us-west2 for 48h with rollback criteria: error rate +> 1% or median latency increase +> 50ms for paid/enterprise
Shadow deployment: duplicate live traffic and compare outputs between fastpath and soft-demote variants to measure semantic delta before enabling routes
Load test: synthetic enterprise burst test to validate escrow refill & preemption mechanics
rollout_plan: Stage 1: feature behind flag, disabled by default. Deploy to staging and run replay tests.
Stage 2: Canary: enable for 5% of free-tier traffic in us-west2 for 48h. Monitor decision metrics and regression alerts.
Stage 3: Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 50% of free-tier over 7 days with manual checkpoints. Keep paid/enterprise on fastpath by default.
Stage 4: Introduce per-customer opt-in experiments for paid plans to evaluate cost/latency trade-offs.
Stage 5: GA with Console controls for thresholds and per-plan overrides.
